newsitem.title: USA: CBOE adds milestone strikes to Dec S&P 500 options.
newsitem.headline: CBOE adds milestone strikes to Dec S&P 500 options.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange on Friday added 1,025 and 1,050 strike prices to its S&P 500 index .SPX index options.
The new strike prices were added only in the December expiration series and give investors the opportunity to buy or sell puts or calls on the SPX with strike levels of 1,025 and 1,050.
The highest strike price in the March series is 900, in the April series it is 875, in May 850, in June 925 and in September 975.
The SPX spot index closed at 793.17 Friday, up 3.61.
The SPX reached an all-time high of 817.68 on February 19.
The four new options -- two calls and two puts -- did not trade.
The SPX December 1,025 call was bid at 2-5/15 and offered at 2-11/16. The December 1,050 call was bid at 1-7/16 and offered at 1-11/16.
The December 1,025 put had a bid/offer of 198/199 and the December 1,050 put had a bid/offer of 221-1/8-222-1/8.
"They didn't make much of an impression," Micheal Schwartz at Oppenheimer & Co said of the new option contracts. "The quotes on the put side are bigger than on some stocks."
Harrison Roth, senior options strategist at Cowen & Co, said he was puzzled by the additions.
"I cannot understand who wants that option which is 225 points out of the money," he said.
